issues.description: The docs excerpt I read did not show hole_pattern's signature; I learned it only from the plate_with_holes example (diameter first, spacing=, count=). I did not read the rest of the docs.
The task gave no hole diameter or positions; I chose 4 mm holes on a 50x30 grid, 4 mm thick plate. Nothing in the tool could help with this.
The hole position in `cad measure --holes` is reported at z=0 (the bottom face) for a drill-from-top hole. This is slightly surprising but harmless.
Task says 'printable' but nothing in docs says what that implies (min wall, hole size, STL units/watertightness). I assumed 4 mm thickness and 4 mm holes 6 mm from the edges.
Hole position in `measure --holes` is reported at z=0 (hole start/bottom) with no clear indication of which end; minor.

The docs excerpt I read never described hole_pattern/hole signatures; I only learned hole_pattern(diameter, spacing=, count=) from `cad examples show plate_with_holes`. I did not read the full docs beyond the first ~150 lines.
Hole at position z=0 with depth 4 reported; fine, but no explicit 'through' indicator in measure --holes.

hole_pattern is not described in `cad docs` output I read (head -150); I only learned its signature (diameter, spacing, count, name) from the bundled plate_with_holes example. Whether spacing is centre-to-centre and whether the pattern is centred was inferred and confirmed only via measure --holes.
I did not render the result; I relied on inspect/measure --holes numbers only.

suggestions.suggestion: Put a minimal 'plate with 4 holes -> STL' recipe in `cad --help` or at the top of `cad docs`.
Say in the docs that hole_pattern is centred on the part origin.
Put a minimal 'plate with holes' snippet at the top of `cad --help` or in the output of `cad init`.
Have `cad init` print the exact commands for build, inspect, export and where the STL ends up.
Have `cad --help` or `cad init` point to `cad docs` and `cad examples` explicitly.
Add a minimal 'plate with 4 holes' snippet at the top of the docs Quick start.
Add a `cad export --format stl` note about watertightness / printability check output.
Put a minimal 'plate with holes -> STL' quickstart at the top of `cad --help` / docs.
Mention in `cad init` output that `cad examples` exists.
Add a printability check (min wall, flat bottom) hint after export.
Put a minimal 'plate with 4 holes' script in the top of `cad --help` or `cad docs`.
Document hole_pattern in the main API table.
Make `cad init` print a hint that it keeps an existing model.py.
